TESLA: Crystal Sun Solar Project, Fort Bend County, TX, August 8th, 2026

This flyover is over the proposed project area for Tesla’s Project Crystal Sun, a planned $10.1 billion solar cell and module manufacturing facility.

It is located in Fort Bend County, Texas, near the intersection of FM 1994 and FM 762. The site covers more than 3,000 acres across multiple parcels, within Lamar Consolidated ISD jurisdiction, roughly 40 minutes south/southeast of the Brookshire, TX, Megafactory.

Visible features include the W.A. Parish Generating Station to the east, Cutlass Solar Farms to the southwest and the Big Creek corridor.

“I want to die on Mars, just not on impact.”
― Elon Musk

"Once you said you want to die on Mars. Why? 

Elon Musk: I don't declare I don't want to die on Mars.

Given the choice of dying on Earth or dying on Mars, I'd say, yeah, I'm sure I'll die on Mars.

But it's not some kind of Mars death wish. And if I do die on Mars, I just don't want it to be on impact."

Musk's point was never about seeking death on Mars. It's about his belief that humanity should become multiplanetary—and that he would rather spend his life helping build that future.

Just put the Model Y L through its paces… and wow.

Took the long-wheelbase 6-seater out for a real drive and it completely reset my expectations. 

That extra stretch in the wheelbase doesn’t just give you actual usable third-row space and captain’s chairs — it makes the whole car feel planted and composed. Corners? 

It hugs them way tighter than a family SUV has any right to. Quiet, refined, and still that classic Tesla punch when you want it.

Then I handed it over to FSD and just supervised. Smooth, confident, zero drama. This thing is legitimately one of the best daily drivers Tesla has ever made.

Six seats. Real space. Still fun as hell to drive.

Elon Musk reveals why Starship became more pointy. 

It turns out the shape was partly inspired by the movie The Dictator.

Musk explained that they thought it would be funny to make the rocket more pointy—and they actually did it.

When asked whether the sharper design improved aerodynamics, Musk said:

"No, nothing."

In fact, he said Starship could be made much blunter and still work fine.

Slightly worse aerodynamically. Way more fun visually. 😎🚀
